2444: Burnout is a state of physical, emotional and mental exhaustion associated with chronic work stress.
2448: Burnout often shows up through three main dimensions:
2449: Individual levelEmotional exhaustionA feeling of physical and mental depletion, lack of energy, emotional wear and tear and difficulty coping with the demands of work and with other people.
2450: Interpersonal levelDepersonalisation or cynicismEmotional distance from work, colleagues or customers, accompanied by irritability, coldness, cynicism or loss of involvement.
2451: Self-assessment levelReduced personal accomplishmentA feeling of ineffectiveness, low professional self-esteem and a perception that work has lost meaning or purpose.
2462: A feeling of emptiness, hopelessness or ineffectiveness
2466: Increased use of alcohol, tobacco or medication
2470: The intervention should focus on strengthening individual, organisational and relational protective resources.
2475: Recognise signs of exhaustion and accept the need to look after yourself
2492: Promote balance between personal and professional life
2494: Invest in meaningful relationships and keep a support network
2496: Assess the need for psychological or medical follow-up
2503: Strengthen interpersonal relationships: promote skills in
2509: Ineffective coping strategies: Emotional suppression, isolation, using work excessively as an escape.
2510: A self-sacrificing mindset: Avoid beliefs such as “If I don’t do it, no one will.”
2511: Neglecting signs of distress: Do not normalise persistent exhaustion or intense distress as “part of the job”.
2512: Excessive perfectionism: Avoid pursuing perfect performance at the expense of wellbeing.
2515: Referral to specialist support should be considered when:
2516: !Symptoms persist daily for several weeks
2517: !There is a significant impact on personal or professional functioning
2518: !There is intense distress, hopelessness or a persistent feeling of emptiness
2519: !There are risk behaviours or suicidal ideation
2520: !Personal resources and informal support are no longer enough
